Apr . . . Jul . . Oct . Dec The Hoppener Haus is the most famous half-timbered house in the German town of Celle. Built in 1532, the six-storied place makes for a picturesque spectacle. Etchings of the solar system and its planets decorate the wooden beams of the house. The facade also bears ornamentations and decorations that mimic reptiles, grotesque faces, comical figures, as well as gods of the planets. On the third floor of the building, one can see the portrait of Duke of Ernest, which was a late addition made in 1901. Right in front of the Hoppener Haus, there is a historical fountain. The installation, which is decorated with a heraldic symbol, is actually among the only three non-potable water fountains that were a part of the water supply system here in the 16th century. The area around the haus is also interesting for visitors as there are a variety of restaurants, bars, and shops to explore.
